As the central funding conduit for all SingHealth Care Integration and Healthier SG initiatives, RHS provides overarching strategic direction to its programmes, supports service development, and monitors and evaluates key population health initiatives. As Director, you will support the Chief Operating Officer of RHS Operations and clinical site leads, working alongside the SingHealth Office of Regional Health (SORH) to implement population health initiatives, guide mid and long-term strategic planning, and put in place the policy, planning and governance framework to support a future-ready health system through an integrated Community of Care (COC) ecosystem. What You Will Do: You will oversee and coordinate the SingHealth Healthier SG team's service delivery and resource deployment within the COC, while reviewing all services operating under the COC and providing advice and governance on operational issues. In the area of operations and strategic planning, you will work with relevant internal and external stakeholders to formulate, implement and review strategies to deliver value-based care to the population in the eastern region. You will drive and coordinate policies that facilitate population enrolment, and engage process owners and business units to establish business insights that support value-based care and capitation pilot initiatives through data analytics. For the implementation of Next Generation Primary Care, you will engage regional General Practitioners (GPs) and Primary Care Networks (PCNs) to adopt care protocols, programmes, IT systems, and care support and financing arrangements. You will plan and facilitate the regional resident enrolment and service journey, and implement integrated community care teams comprising primary care providers, community nurses, care coordinators and community partners to support residents in adhering to treatment and sustaining behavioural changes that improve their health outcomes. On corporate oversight and governance, you will act as the primary liaison for RHS matters between sites and the RHS group with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), put in place a planning and governance framework to enable monitoring and accountability of key stakeholders, and establish a Risk Management framework to govern the programmes. In the area of performance monitoring and programme evaluation, you will work closely with SingHealth RHS stakeholders to develop key performance indicators, review the progress and effectiveness of RHS initiatives, and recommend improvement plans. Together with Strategic Finance, you will evaluate the cost-effectiveness of right-siting efforts and drive the implementation of the national population health strategy in the capitation funding model to support whole-population enrolment within the eastern region. You will also provide leadership in data analytics to identify needs and areas for improvement. As a partner engagement leader, you will build strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to improve health across all age groups, work with sites and institutions to establish system enablers aligned to the cluster's population health strategy, and cultivate strong partnerships with community partners and agencies including MOH, AIC and social and community organisations to drive programmes that promote healthy lifestyle choices. You will also contribute to manpower development by working with the Group Director to develop training programmes that build a core team of staff well versed in population health, and grow a credible pool of staff with competencies and subject matter expertise in this domain. The hallmark of Phase 2, the TTSH Medical Tower will add approximately 600 acute beds, significantly strengthening TTSH's healthcare capacity for high-intensity, specialist care. It will house an expanded Emergency Department, additional operating theatres, and procedural suites, and specialist outpatient clinics, all purpose-designed to advance frailty-ready and technology-enabled care. We operate more than 2,000 beds and provide care across more than 60 clinical disciplines . We are looking for an experienced and motivated Senior Manager/Asst Director to join Operations (Medicine), supporting selected Clinical Department(s) within the Division of Medicine in an acute tertiary hospital. What You will Do: In this role, you will work closely with the Director, Operations, Clinical Heads of Department (HODs) and senior stakeholders to plan, develop and implement clinical services and care models across Medicine disciplines. You will translate clinical intent and service plans into well‑designed, practical and sustainable operational solutions, working in close collaboration with Service Operations and MEC Operations teams to ensure readiness and smooth integration into ongoing services. You will play an important role in driving service development and access improvement efforts, redesigning patient journeys and operational workflows to meet service needs, organisational targets and NHG priority areas. This role requires active leadership and ownership, from planning and coordination through implementation, review and refinement. As a Senior Manager/Asst Director, you will lead cross‑disciplinary initiatives, apply data and operational insights to support planning and performance review, and provide clear reports and updates to department, division, organisation and cluster‑level stakeholders on progress, risks and outcomes. You will also be responsible for supervising, coaching and developing the Ops Med team, building capability in clinical operations support, analytics and stakeholder management. The role involves regular engagement with clinicians, Service Operations, MEC Operations, corporate services and external stakeholders, offering meaningful exposure to service development and improvement work across multiple Medicine specialties. What We're Looking For: Bachelor’s degree in any discipline. At least 10–12 years of relevant experience, preferably in healthcare operations, clinical services development or hospital administration, including people management responsibilities. Experience working with senior clinicians or professional leaders to plan and implement clinical services or programmes in a tertiary care setting is an advantage. Strong leadership and execution skills, with ability to drive initiatives from planning through implementation. Good analytical and problem‑solving skills, with experience using data to support operational planning and performance monitoring. Experience in supervising, coaching and developing team members. Proficient in Microsoft Office, with intermediate‑level Excel skills (e.g. formulas, pivot tables, basic data analysis). Good written, communication and presentation skills (English). Institution All Job Function All Job ID All Employment Type All Clear Search Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource, NUHS@Home Job ID: 10537 Job Function: Administration Institution: National University Health System Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource, NUHS@Home About NUHS@Home NUHS@Home is the National University Health System’s Virtual Campus, a premise-neutral care environment that brings healthcare services beyond the four walls of the hospital and into homes, clinics, community settings, and digital spaces. It serves as the organising platform for multiple virtual and distributed care models, enabling patients to access the right care, at the right time, in the right place. Since its inception in 2020, NUHS@Home has rapidly grown into a critical pillar of NUHS’ vision for healthcare that is integrated, agile, and closer to the patient. More than a single service, it represents a new architecture for care delivery – one where geography no longer dictates access, and recovery happens where patients feel safest, supported, and most at home. The Role We are seeking an experienced, strategic and forward-thinking Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource . Reporting to the Head of Human Resource, you will serve as a trusted HR leader and strategic business partner to the NUHS@Home leadership team and key stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys driving people strategies that support workforce transformation, talent development, employee engagement and organisational growth, while leading the HR team and providing tactical advice and practical solutions across the employee lifecycle. As a key member of the NUHS@Home leadership team, you will play an important role in shaping the people agenda and enabling the continued growth and evolution of the NUHS@Home care delivery model. You will also contribute to leadership continuity for the HR function by supporting the Head of Human Resource on designated matters and strengthening succession coverage within the HR team. What you will own Strategic HR Business Partnering Build strong, trusted relationships with business leaders and stakeholders, providing strategic advice and practical HR solutions that support organisational priorities and business outcomes. Advise leaders on the interpretation and application of HR policies and procedures, employment legislation, performance management, manpower planning, resourcing, rewards and other people-related matters. Partner with Talent Acquisition to develop and implement targeted recruitment strategies aligned with NUHS@Home manpower plans, workforce requirements and growth priorities, including the review and approval of compensation recommendations. Lead the annual manpower planning and budgeting exercise, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, workforce requirements and financial objectives. Support organisational transformation, change management and workforce redesign initiatives to enable the growth and evolution of NUHS@Home’s care delivery model. Analyse workforce trends, employee engagement data, attrition metrics and other manpower indicators to generate insights and recommendations for organisational and workforce planning, and the effective management of organisational risks. Oversee employee lifecycle matters through the HR team, including employee enquiries, employment changes, transfers, appointments and exit processes, in accordance with HR policies and procedures. People Leadership and Development Lead, manage and develop the HR team to ensure the effective, professional and timely delivery of HR plans, programmes, processes and services. Provide direction, coaching and support to build HR capability, strengthen service delivery and promote a high-performing team culture. Foster close collaboration with relevant Group HR Centres of Excellence to deliver integrated and value-adding people solutions. Employee Engagement, Talent and Workforce Development Drive employee engagement initiatives that strengthen workplace culture, employee experience, productivity and retention. Work with leaders to identify organisational capability gaps and support organisation design, workforce planning, capability-building and talent pipeline initiatives. Promote a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, accountability and service excellence. Governance, Policy and Stakeholder Collaboration Collaborate with NUHS Group HR Centres of Excellence and relevant stakeholders to implement HR projects, programmes and initiatives. Work with the Centres of Excellence to review and enhance HR policies, guidelines and processes to ensure their relevance to NUHS@Home and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. Contribute to NUHS, Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Health (MOH), MOH Holdings (MOHH), NUHS@Home and Human Resource projects, events, governance initiatives, policy reviews and committees, as assigned or appointed. Who You Are This role is suited to an experienced HR leader who is able to operate at both strategic and operational levels: shaping the people agenda, advising senior stakeholders, leading a small HR team, and translating organisational priorities into practical workforce and talent solutions. Background A bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management or a related discipline. At least 10 years of relevant HR experience, preferably within the healthcare sector, with a strong track record in HR business partnering, organisational transformation, workforce redesign and people management. Demonstrated ability to influence and partner with business leaders to achieve strategic business and people outcomes. Demonstrated experience leading, coaching and developing HR professionals or business partners. Strong knowledge of HR practices, including employee relations, performance management, manpower planning, talent management, resourcing and rewards. Proven leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to develop team members, build effective partnerships across functions and work independently with a high degree of initiative. Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to translate workforce data and insights into actionable recommendations. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, with experience in workforce analytics, manpower reporting, budgeting and presentation development. Experience in healthcare operations, change management or organisational capability-building would be an advantage. What we offer An opportunity to help shape NUHS’ healthcare workforce of the future and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore. Meaningful ownership and decision-making responsibility in a high-growth healthcare transformation programme. The opportunity to contribute to the development of NUHS@Home and its future leadership capability as the programme scales. Why Join Us NUHS@Home is redefining care delivery by creating Singapore’s virtual campus for comprehensive clinical care through a digital-first approach. You will contribute to workforce transformation and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore and beyond. The role works closely with clinical, corporate, and other stakeholders to drive standardisation, collaboration, commercial optimisation, and continuous improvement across the Group. The role is responsible for developing and implementing effective procurement and contract management strategies across the assigned groupings, ensuring that procurement activities are aligned with organisational priorities, deliver value for money, manage commercial and supply risks, and optimise supplier performance. Responsibilities 1) Contract Planning & Strategy Lead the development and implementation of contract planning and strategy. Identify opportunities for Group-wide demand aggregation, standardisation, and commercial optimisation. Monitor market developments, supplier trends, emerging technologies, and supply risks. Provide strategic advice to senior management and stakeholders on contract and commercial matters. 2) Procurement & Sourcing Oversee the procurement activities, ensuring robust, transparent, and effective procurement processes. Provide direction on sourcing strategies, tender approaches, evaluation methodologies, and commercial models. Work with stakeholders to develop appropriate specifications, evaluation criteria, and contractual requirements. Ensure appropriate governance and compliance throughout the procurement process. Ensure procurement activities achieve optimal outcomes in terms of value, quality, risk, and total cost of ownership. 3) Contract Management & Performance Provide oversight of the effective management of contracts. Drive supplier performance, service improvements, cost containment, and resolution of contractual issues. Monitor contract performance, commercial outcomes, risks, and key obligations. Ensure timely contract reviews, renewals, extensions, variations and exits. Identify opportunities to leverage contracts across institutions and strengthen Group-level commercial outcomes. 4) Stakeholder & Supplier Management Develop effective relationships with clinical, corporate, operational and Group stakeholders to understand requirements and drive effective procurement and contract outcomes. Establish effective supplier relationships while maintaining appropriate commercial governance and accountability. 5) “Surgical” Grouping Provide leadership for procurement and contract management relating to surgical requirements. Work closely with clinical stakeholders to balance clinical requirements, patient safety, operational needs, and commercial considerations. Promote appropriate standardisation and rationalisation of products and suppliers, where clinically and operationally appropriate. Develop strong supplier and market intelligence for surgical categories. 6) “Non-Clinical & Corporate” Grouping Provide leadership for procurement and contract management of non-clinical and corporate requirements, including non-clinical equipment and services. Identify opportunities to consolidate demand, standardise requirements and improve commercial outcomes across institutions. Work with relevant specialist Group functions to ensure clear ownership, appropriate interfaces and effective governance for categories that intersect with their areas of responsibility. Develop the Group's capabilities and portfolio for non-clinical and corporate procurement as the scope of GVCM evolves. 7) Team Leadership & Capability Development Lead, develop and motivate staff. Build category and contract management capabilities, commercial acumen, and professional expertise within the team. Promote collaboration and knowledge sharing across GVCM. 8) Transformation & Continuous Improvement Drive continuous improvement in procurement and contract management processes, systems, tools, and practices. Identify opportunities for digitalisation, automation, data-driven decision-making, and improved contract visibility. Support the development and implementation of GVCM frameworks, policies, playbooks, and standards. Lead or contribute to Group-wide transformation initiatives relating to procurement, vendor, and contract management. Required Competencies and Qualifications • Degree in procurement, supply chain management, business, finance, or a related discipline. • Minimum 10 years of professional experience in procurement, contract management, strategic sourcing, and/or vendor management, preferably in a healthcare, public sector, or large institutional environment. • Demonstrated experience managing complex and high-value procurement and contractual portfolios. • Strong commercial, negotiation, analytical and stakeholder management capabilities. • Experience in leading teams and developing procurement and contract management capabilities. • Demonstrated ability to work across organisational boundaries and influence senior stakeholders. Family Intervention Division develop and review policies which enhance intervention, stability and resilience of youth-at-risk and vulnerable families (including those with problem gamblers). You will be part of a team of officers who will be working with other Ministries and Divisions within MSF and our stakeholders to formulate and conceptualise comprehensive family service policies and programmes. In particular, your work on family services targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families and individuals will focus on designing systems and policies that intervene upstream and downstream to influence family functioning, reduce risk and strengthen protective factors. Your responsibilities as a Assistant Director (Family Intervention) will include: • Collaborate with external stakeholders and partners across Ministries and Divisions to formulate, implement and evaluate family service policies targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families. • Work closely with policy, operations and practice divisions within MSF to ensure seamless integration between policy development, service delivery and frontline practice, facilitating regular coordination and alignment across different functional areas. • Conceptualise and design upstream and downstream intervention systems that influence family functioning, reduce risk factors and strengthen protective factors. • Conduct policy research and analysis to inform evidence-based approaches to family service delivery and intervention strategies. • Plan and carry out stakeholder engagement activities with partners, service providers and other stakeholders/beneficiary groups to ensure responsive policy development. • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of family service policies and programmes, using data analysis to inform continuous improvement and refinement. • [If given supervisory responsibilities] Lead a team of officers to carry out the above responsibilities. The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) seeks to transform Singapore into a leading global city of talent, enterprise and innovation. Our mission is to promote economic growth and create good jobs to enable Singaporeans to improve their lives. The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and safeguards Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena. At the Europe (EUR) Division, our mission is to grow and safeguard our external economic space for Singaporeans and Singapore companies by strengthening connectivity and interoperability with overseas markets, as well as building economic resilience and adaptability, through economic cooperation with Europe. The evolving trade landscape and recent global developments require us to continually innovate and adapt our strategies for economic engagement with partners in Europe. We have broadened our focus, to address new opportunities and challenges such as the digital and green economies as well as supply chain resilience. We are actively developing and implementing novel trade tools such as Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) and Green Economy Agreements (GEAs), as well as establishing new economic platforms to strengthen institutional linkages between Singapore and our key markets. Our larger vision is to update Singapore’s playbook for international economic engagement, and contribute towards a future-ready economy with growth opportunities for our people and companies. We are expanding our team in line with efforts to ensure that we continue to achieve our mission. You will wear at least four hats: (i) trade diplomat; (ii) trade negotiator; (iii) trade policy analyst; and (iv) account manager for a diverse range of local and foreign government, industry and people sector stakeholders. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Oct 2026. METI’s Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division plays a key role in creating an energy system that is secure, resilient, cost-competitive, and ready to transition to a low carbon future. Our work keeps the lights on today, and builds the power system for tomorrow. Energy is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. Recent energy crises due to the war in Ukraine and ongoing conflict in the Middle East have upended the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they struggle with energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. At the same time, our energy system is an enabler for economic growth, as speed to power is critical to capture strategic and economically significant investments. Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy system that safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism. METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in ensuring energy remains a key enabler of Singapore’s competitiveness, climate goals and national resilience via the five ‘Cs’: • Confidence. Ensure our system resilience continues to be a source of confidence for our people, through multiple lines of defence to safeguard energy security, resilience, and reliability. These include diversifying our fuel sources and strengthening our fuel reserves. • Competitiveness. Harness energy to bolster our economic competitiveness, through scaling our generation and grid capacity to meet growing needs and attract electricity-intensive investments. This also involves reviewing our energy system planning models and leveraging flexibility assets to secure speed to power while maintaining system reliability. • Carbon. Ensure our power system infrastructure and electricity market are ready for a low-carbon future to meet our climate commitments. Infrastructure and markets are critical to ensuring Singapore can pursue every possible pathway to develop a diversified and affordable portfolio of low-carbon energy options. • Connectivity. Deepen connectivity with our partners and ensure new imported energy sources can enter Singapore’s grid and electricity market. • Costs. Keep costs in check to ensure we strike the right balance in the energy transition. This involves right-pricing energy and infrastructure, and ensuring our market frameworks continue to support a competitive and commercially sustainable generation sector. Your responsibilities include one or more of the following workstreams: • Formulate robust strategies and policies to regulate and develop the gas and electricity sectors. This involves working with key stakeholders to develop and implement regulatory and market structures, to strike a balance among our objectives of economic competitiveness, energy security and environmental sustainability. • Formulate and review strategies and policies to enhance our energy security by diversifying Singapore’s energy sources, including those for electricity and gas imports. • Formulate and review policies and strategies to develop supporting enablers for the electricity and gas sectors, including infrastructure
